verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's virtual keys let admins issue scoped credentials that restrict model access, set spend/budget caps, rate limits (rpm_limit), and team/user scoping, and MCP access can be controlled per key/team — this directly supports issuing least-privilege credentials for an agent. missing for 10: no explicit fine-grained permission model beyond model/spend/rate limits (e.g., action-level or tool-level scoping outside MCP), and no independent/hands-on verification of key scoping working as documented in production.
